correctness.rationale: The proof covers every Euclidean stadium with a>0, r>0 and all Euclidean rectangles without orientation or translation restrictions. Central symmetry replaces each rectangle by a congruent centered one. Each centered rectangle corresponds to two equal-radius diagonal vertices, so the exact two-arc geometry of stadium-circle intersections controls all possible rotations, including the full-circle and square regimes. The unique axis-parallel maximum follows from the strictly decreasing derivative numerator r²-a u-2u², with the resulting optimizer in the strict x>y regime and all contacts on circular caps; this proves global orientation and center uniqueness. The relation st+2t²=1 reduces the perimeter and filling profiles to exact rational-algebraic functions. Symbolic derivatives show a unique normalized-perimeter maximum at t=2/π and strict monotonicity of filling. Actual standalone checker paths were run; exact symbolic identities and feasible-orientation numerical comparisons passed. Finite tests are corroboration, not universal proof.

originality.rationale: The full 2019 Behroozi manuscript already supplies centeredness of maximum-area rectangles in centrally symmetric convex bodies, so that known fact is excluded from the novelty claim. The theorem instead proves orientation rigidity for all noncircular stadiums, the exact unrestricted rectangle-area profile, a sharp and uniquely attained perimeter-normalized bound with a noncircular extremizer, and strictly invertible filling fraction. Closest published rectangle algorithms concern general convex optimization or polygonal containers; their statements do not give these explicit stadium formulas. No verified primary source or indexed published theorem was found to imply the full statement. Historical completeness remains provisional.

value.rationale: Largest inscribed rectangle capacity of a convex body is a standard motivated approximation functional. Within the canonical one-parameter family of Minkowski segment-plus-disk shapes, unrestricted orientation might a priori change the extremizer. The result gives a complete shape-wise classification and strict rigidity; its sharp fixed-perimeter maximizer is unexpectedly a noncircular stadium instead of the disk. A distinct normalized rectangle-to-container area fraction is strictly invertible, yielding geometric shape recovery from a scalar capacity measurement. The specific parameter is intrinsic to the natural full family and both exact optimum and inverse are non-implied by known centeredness or polygon algorithms. It is more than a routine evaluation of a fixed-orientation rectangle.
